newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house panel passes re-election bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house panel passes re-election bill.

text.p: A special committee of the Brazilian lower house Wednesday approved a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to seek re-election, officials said.
Panel officials said deputies voted 19 to 11 to pass the constitutional amendment, which has been embroiled in controversy and threatened even to split the government's supporters in Congress.
The lower house committee has still to vote on more than 20 proposed amendments but government leaders said they were confident they could defeat them all.

The constitutional amendment allowing re-election of sitting presidents, governors and mayors must now pass through two rounds of voting on the full floor of the Chamber of Deputies, where it faces its real test.
Government leaders had been hoping to put it to a vote in the chamber next week but even they were acknowledging Wednesday that would be ambitious.
Michel Temer, the pro-government lower house leader of Brazil's largest party, the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), said it would take time to sort out his deputies stance.

The PMDB has become a bit of a thorn in the side of the government's re-election aims since party delegates voted last Sunday to obstruct progress of the bill until elections for the presidencies of the upper and lower houses were over.
"There's no way we can put it to a vote (on the floor) now. There's a lot of negotiation still to be done," Temer's spokesman quoted him as saying.
